_comment: Which release of the Redrob Group Design System this browser is built against.
The browser cannot import the package: its window chrome is C++ and its WebUI is built by
build_webui from files in the source tree, so there is no node_modules at build time and no
resolver to ask. The values therefore have to be COPIED in -- and a copy with no pin is how two
products end up claiming the same brand while painting different colours.
integrity is pinned as well as version because it is the only part a registry cannot restate. A
published npm version is immutable, so a tarball whose hash stops matching is a tampered or
corrupted fetch rather than a new release, and scripts/vendor_design_system.py refuses it.
gitHead is the commit in redrob-labs/redrob-ui that produced this release. It is recorded so a
colour can be traced to the source that decided it, not just to a version number.
To move to a new release: edit version, clear integrity, run
python3 scripts/vendor_design_system.py --update --accept-new-integrity
and commit the pin together with the regenerated files. Never edit the vendored files by hand.
The font files are here for the same reason as the values. design_tokens.css declares sixteen
@font-face rules pointing at fonts/, and a rule whose file is missing does not fail a build -- the
browser requests it, gets nothing, and silently renders in a different typeface. Listed are exactly
the families --font-sans and --font-mono can select: Pretendard's six weights, then Wanted Sans and
Noto Sans Devanagari, which the sans stack falls through to for a glyph Pretendard does not carry.
The serif and display cuts are deliberately NOT vendored: no stylesheet in this browser names
--font-serif, --font-serif-display or their Korean pairs, so shipping them would be 1.2 MB of
typeface in three bundles that nothing can reach. scripts/check_design_tokens.py holds that line.
design_system.css is the COMPONENT layer -- 145 `.rr-*` classes over 2,017 rules. It is vendored for the same
reason as the tokens and with one extra constraint: it must be linked AFTER design_tokens.css,
because it is not only components. It corrects three roles the token sheet declares first
(--ink-muted on both themes, --surface-sunken on dark) and adds six more (--series-*, --tex-*,
--rake-*, --dia-rake). In the design system's own order the correction wins; linked the other way
round the browser would paint the superseded values and nothing would report it. Gate check 7
holds that order.
It also carries rules that are NOT namespaced: ::selection, ::backdrop, li::marker, the
-webkit-autofill group, caret-color and accent-color on :root, and word-break for :lang(ko) and
hi. Those are intended -- they are the part of a page a class cannot reach -- but they are why
this file is a decision rather than an inert copy, and why the WebUI screens are captured after
adding it.
preflight.css is deliberately NOT vendored. It is the design system's optional page-owner sheet
(html background, color-scheme, body font, a focus ring), and chrome_base.css is already this
browser's own version of exactly that, written against Chromium's constraints. Two sheets both
claiming `html` is the shadowing defect check 3 exists to catch.
_brand_assets_comment: brand_assets is a SEPARATE pin from the npm package above, because the artwork has a different
source. @redrob-labs/ui deliberately ships no logo file: its Mark component takes src and darkSrc
as props, so the host supplies the files. The files come from the design system delivery, which is
not a registry -- there is nothing to fetch and no version to resolve, so these are recorded by
sha256 and by their path in the delivery instead.
What the hash is FOR: 10-logo.md says the artwork is 'Never redrawn, restretched, recolored or
otherwise modified', and lists recoloring, substituting the gradient and adding an effect (shadow,
outline, blur) under Incorrect usage. A brand file is the one asset in this tree that a well-meaning
edit ruins silently -- nudge the blue, flatten the gradient, re-export at a smaller size, and every
gate still passes because nothing in a build reads a PNG's pixels. The hash is what fails.
Why TWO files and not one recolored one: assets/Symbol/README.md assigns each variant a ground.
redrob-symbol.png is the brand gradient and belongs on white and light grounds; solid-white is flat
white and belongs on redrob-black and dark surfaces. A single file cannot serve both -- the
gradient symbol on the dark page measured 1.00:1 against its own ground -- and painting one file
through a CSS mask in a token colour is the recolor the spec forbids. So the page ships both and
swaps them on data-theme, which is exactly what the design system's own .rr-mark rules do.
To move to new artwork: replace the files from the delivery and update the hashes here in the same
commit. Never edit a file under brand/.
_derived_comment: `files` below are byte copies of the release. `derived` is the one artifact this script TRANSFORMS,
and it is kept separate so nobody mistakes a generated file for a copy.
The design system ships its 252 glyphs as a React module. This browser's WebUI is TypeScript under
Trusted Types with no React, no bundler and no node_modules at build time, and assigning innerHTML
there throws -- so a glyph cannot be imported, and its geometry has to arrive as DATA in the source
tree before the build, exactly as the stylesheets and the fonts do.
What was there before: 16 glyphs drawn by hand at 16x16 with ROUND caps at stroke 1.3 to 1.6.
45-icons.md specifies a 24x24 box on a 20px live area, stroke 2 unscaled, butt caps ('Never round'),
miter joins at limit 3 and every diagonal at 40 degrees, and the delivery ships 252 glyphs on exactly
that geometry. Nothing enforced it, so the hand-drawn set had been drifting from the brand since it
was written -- and two glyphs were recorded as having no design-system equivalent which, on a re-read
of the spec's own group table, they do. Gate check 9 now fails on any hand-drawn glyph.
The transform is deliberately narrow: it copies every attribute verbatim, never reformatting a
coordinate, and it REFUSES rather than emit a glyph whose element count does not match the source --
a dropped path is a glyph that still draws, which is the failure nobody would see.
